title: IUPAC Naming: Root, Suffix and Prefix
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
objective: How a chemical name is built from a molecule: the root counts the parent chain's carbons, the suffix gives its bonds and principal group, and the prefix names what is attached.

fill.q: The root word for a parent chain of three carbons is ____.
The primary suffix for a chain with only C–C single bonds is ____.
The secondary suffix for an alcohol is ____.
A CH₃– group attached to the parent chain is named ____.
The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CHO is ____.

tf.q: The root word depends on the number of carbons in the parent chain.
The suffix -ene shows a C≡C triple bond.
In propan-1-ol the "e" of propane is dropped before -ol.
tf.explain: It is dropped before a suffix that starts with a vowel.

tf.q: The chain is numbered so that the principal group gets the highest locant.

ar.r: Its C=O group is inside the carbon chain.

ar.a: Butan-2-ol is numbered from the end nearer the OH group.
ar.r: The principal group must get the lowest locant.

mcq.q: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ is:
Which prefix names a Cl atom on the chain?
mcq.explain: Halogens are named fluoro, chloro, bromo, iodo.

mcq.q: The IUPAC name of CH₂=CHCH₃ is:
The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂OH is:

num.q: How many carbon atoms are in the parent chain of 2-methylbutane?
steps: but = 4 carbons in the parent chain

num.q: What is the locant of the OH group in butan-2-ol?

short.q: Explain each part of the name 2-methylpropan-1-ol.
short.solution: 2-methyl: CH₃ branch on C2 (prefix); prop: 3-carbon parent chain (root); an: all single bonds (primary suffix); 1-ol: OH on C1 (secondary suffix).
